long_biography.plain_text:
After studying business at the University of San Diego and New York University, Lorenzo Fertitta joined his family's Las Vegas enterprise and became president of Station Casinos. He and his brother Frank expanded the locals-focused casino business, navigated a restructuring and later returned it to public markets as Red Rock Resorts.

Their most consequential move came in 2001, when the brothers paid $2 million for the Ultimate Fighting Championship and placed it within Zuffa. Fertitta led the organization as chairman and chief executive, professionalizing operations, widening regulatory acceptance and building international distribution. The investment's eventual multibillion-dollar sale established UFC as the defining value-creation chapter of his career.
